items.name: xcl
items.description: Xbox Series compatibility layer for Windows - runs console game code natively, reimplements the console system libraries and recompiles RDNA2 shaders to DXIL

readme.excerpt:
XCL is a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X S (GDK) games you own on a Windows PC - in the spirit of Wine/Proton. There is no CPU emulation: the game's x64 code runs natively, and XCL provides its own, independently written implementations of the console system libraries the PC does not have ( kernelx.dll , XGameRuntime, d3d12 xs.dll , …). The console's GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL).

XCL works only on unpacked game files you already own. It does not download, decrypt or unpack game packages (XVC / MSIXVC) and contains nothing for circumventing DRM. The repository holds no code, headers or binaries from the console SDK, no keys and no game data; the Windows components XCL relies on (XGameRuntime, XAudio2, D3D12, DXC) come from your own system or the public Windows SDK and are not distributed with XCL.

- 100 % of a retail game's shaders translate – all 26 698 RDNA2 programs (26 503 records) of its shader pack become HLSL; random samples compile to DXIL with 0 errors. - The game's own console DLLs run on the PC – its Bink 2 video codec decodes the game's movies, its ray-tracing BVH builder builds acceleration structures on a PC GPU, the AMD FSR 4 console upscaler runs a whole frame on a PC GPU, the GDK HTTP library initialises. - Console textures decode exactly – the GFX10 tiling and mip layout reproduce 909 of 912 textures of the game's texture archive byte for byte, its volume textures included. - 370+ automated tests , in

Build • Docker • Structure • Screenshots [ Українська ] [ česky ] [ 中文 ] [ Magyar ] [ Español ] [ فارسی ] [ Français ] [ Deutsch ] [ Polski ] [ Indonesian ] [ Suomi ] [ മലയാളം ] [ 日本語 ] [ Nederlands ] [ Italiano ] [ Русский ] [ Português (Portugal) ] [ Português (Brasil) ] [ Esperanto ] [ 한국어 ] [ العربي ] [ Tiếng Việt ] [ Dansk ] [ Ελληνικά ] [ Türkçe ] [ Norsk ] [ Română ] [ ქართული ] We need your help to translate this README, RustDesk UI and RustDesk Doc to your native language

Yet another remote desktop solution, written in Rust. Works out of the box with no configuration required. You have full control of your data, with no concerns about security. You can use our rendezvous/relay server, set up your own, or write your own rendezvous/relay server.

RustDesk welcomes contribution from everyone. See CONTRIBUTING.md for help getting started.
features: Prepare your Rust development env and C++ build env
Install vcpkg, and set VCPKG ROOT env variable correctly
Windows: vcpkg install libvpx:x64-windows-static libyuv:x64-windows-static opus:x64-windows-static aom:x64-windows-static
Linux/macOS: vcpkg install libvpx libyuv opus aom
run cargo run
libs/hbb common : config, tcp/udp wrapper, and some other utility functions shared with the server
libs/base : protobuf, fs functions for file transfer, keyboard and platform code used only by this app
libs/scrap : screen capture and video codecs

items.description: An open-source cross-platform alternative to AirDrop

readme.excerpt:
[Homepage][homepage] • [Discord][discord] • [GitHub][github] • [Codeberg][codeberg]

LocalSend is a free, open-source app that allows you to securely share files and messages with nearby devices over your local network without needing an internet connection.
